corrections: The EADB setup routine continues past the early return at 0x5249BD through 0x524A8B. It also allocates and initializes a bit array and computes a derived float; the table bindings alone do not describe the complete routine.

A bad EADB signature or version clears object field +0x44. A zero required count at header +0x0C, +0x18 or +0x14 returns false without clearing that field. These different failure side effects should be preserved when testing original behavior.
The note's successful authoring checks and reported owner videos do not establish original loader equivalence, the collision branch taken at runtime, or recovery of original source.

findings.hint: Recover the complete x86 thiscall EADB setup method, including both failure paths, conditional table binding, allocation, initialization and the final floating-point calculation.
evidence: ECX is saved as the object pointer; object +0x3C supplies the buffer, initially copied to +0x44. The routine checks magic EADB and version 0x26.
Required header DWORDs +0x0C, +0x18 and +0x14 must be nonzero. Header +0x10 controls whether object +0x4C receives base plus header +0x48 or zero.
Object fields +0x48, +0x50, +0x54, +0x58, +0x5C and +0x60 receive base plus header offsets +0x44, +0x54, +0x4C, +0x58, +0x5C and +0x60 respectively.
The success path allocates (header[+0x14] >> 3) + 1 bytes, fills them with 0xFF, copies header +0x7C to object +0x68, and stores a square-root result at +0x6C. Original data at 0xA06508 is float 0.5.
The inspected native registry, recovered source and coverage searches found no exact address reference. The original executable SHA-256 agrees with the note.
dependencies: Allocation entry 0x8F87C8 and its target 0x8F8C42; characterize allocation and failure behavior.
0x8F8D7E imports memset; 0x426D60 calls the _libm_sse2_sqrt_precise import through 0x8F8D60.
A readable EADB buffer and writable object with fields through +0x6C; original floating-point operation order and 32-bit pointer arithmetic.
validation_plan: Compare direct original and candidate calls on valid fixtures, bad magic, bad version, each zero required count, both +0x10 branches and bit-array size boundaries.
Compare the return byte, all object fields and canaries, allocation size, initialized bytes and floating-point result; instrument the original allocator and imports.
Test unusual floating-point values and allocation failure only after establishing a safe harness and the allocator's actual contract.
limits: No differential execution was performed. The table names and allocator semantics were not independently established.
The original performs no visible buffer-length checks in this routine; malformed offsets require controlled memory fixtures.
The registry and source search was address-based and does not rule out equivalent recovery under an unrelated name.

findings.hint: Recover the complete 115-byte IL method as a small node-name-to-index lookup. Preserve case-insensitive comparisons, repeated matches and untouched fields for absent names.
evidence: IL_0000–IL_000E derives the name-vector count from its begin and end pointers; IL_0010–IL_0070 iterates it.
IL_0017–IL_005F performs three independent _stricmp calls for electric, zone_front and zone_back and copies the corresponding index-vector element to object offsets +4, +8 and +12.
The final return is IL_0072; the matrix vector and format arguments are unused in the inspected body.
dependencies: Original _stricmp behavior and string data, 32-bit vector layouts, readable name pointers and a sufficiently long parallel index vector.
validation_plan: Compare original IL execution with the candidate for empty input, mixed case, unrelated names, each recognized name, duplicate names and prefilled object fields.
Compare all object bytes and verify that duplicate names select the last matching index and absent names leave their fields unchanged.
limits: No managed differential harness was run, and behavior on invalid vectors or null names is untested.
Address searches do not establish whether a semantically equivalent implementation already exists under another name.

findings.hint: Use these methods as future collision recovery leads, after mapping the collision-device, vector and physics-body interfaces; do not treat the fitted Impala hull as original behavior.
evidence: In init, IL_014C–IL_0188 calls elPhysFile.exists, branches to setShape_file when present, and otherwise calls loadHzascCollision.

loadHzascCollision has 485 bytes of IL at RVA 0x0028AA68. Its inspected body calls a collision-device virtual entry, adjusts and appends vertices, calls setShape_hull at IL_01A4, and includes cleanup and reference-count operations.
dependencies: Physics-file existence and shape interfaces, collision-device virtual dispatch, model resources, vertex-vector allocation and cleanup, reference counting and elPhysBody shape calls.
validation_plan: Trace both resource-existence branches with original resources and instrument shape calls, vertex arguments, object mutations and cleanup.
Compare the complete method against any candidate with controlled collision-device fixtures and exceptional paths.
limits: Only selected IL regions were inspected; complete field layouts, branch behavior and executable differential tests remain unresolved.
The reported video does not identify the selected collision resource or prove contact geometry.

review.summary: Approved as assembly-reference evidence only for VA 0x5249a0–0x524a8b, with zero source-recovery credit. The complete routine continues beyond the first return: it binds relative offsets, allocates and fills a byte array, and computes a square root. Bad magic or version clears object field +0x44; a zero required count returns false with that field still set. Table meanings, allocation failure, malformed buffers and floating-point edge behavior remain unvalidated. The research note’s mod and runtime claims were not verified.
review.reason: Independent disassembly confirms the entry follows the preceding function’s return, both internal branches and returns stay within the 236-byte range, and padding and a new function follow it. The symbolic transcription preserves the observed instructions, calls, branches and register/stack behavior. An independent assembly and link at the original VA produced 236 bytes identical to the corresponding unmasked Game.exe bytes; the executable, source and output hashes also match the receipts. The two stated callers and external call targets were counterchecked. This establishes assembly-reference equality, not reconstructed source or behavioral equivalence.
